children.name: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
children.blurb: Local and air-gapped model deployment means running AI models on hardware controlled by the law firm or legal department, with no connection to outside networks.

children.name: Secure Storage and Networking for Legal Data
children.blurb: Secure storage and networking for legal data covers the systems, controls, and network paths that keep client matter files, evidence, contracts, and privileged communications confidential, intact, and available to authorized people.

children.name: Timekeeping and Billing Narratives
children.blurb: Timekeeping and billing narratives are the short descriptions a lawyer attaches to each time entry to explain the work performed for a client.

children.name: Firm Knowledge Management
children.blurb: Firm knowledge management covers how a law firm or legal department captures, organizes, retrieves, and reuses its institutional knowledge, including prior work product, research memos, clause libraries, matter histories, and internal expertise.

children.name: Client Intake and Triage
children.blurb: Client intake and triage in legal operations covers the structured capture of a prospective client's matter details, conflict checks, matter classification, urgency scoring, and routing to the right practice team or resource.

sections.body: Legal operations, infrastructure and security is the part of an AI lawyer practice that handles how models are run, how data is protected, how time is recorded, how firm knowledge is stored, and how new clients enter the system. In practice, firms are running smaller open weight models on their own servers or in private cloud accounts, with some using fully air gapped setups for sensitive matters. Secure networking means encrypted connections, role based access, and audit logs rather than a single product. Billing systems now draft narrative entries from calendar, email and document activity, but a human still edits them. Knowledge management uses retrieval over the firm's own precedents and memos, and client intake tools sort incoming requests by practice area and urgency. Among the 732 AI tools tracked on this site, the ones in this section are those aimed at running a law firm rather than arguing a case.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of this work is uneven. Local and air gapped deployment is feasible for a competent IT team, but it is not turnkey, and updates, monitoring and model serving still require real engineering effort. Secure storage and networking for legal data is largely solved at the level of encryption and access control, yet the weak points are usually configuration mistakes and third party integrations, not the core technology. Timekeeping and billing narratives are good enough to produce a first draft, but they miss context and can misstate what happened, so every entry still needs review. Firm knowledge management has moved from keyword search to semantic search, but retrieval can return outdated or irrelevant text, and the system will not tell you when it is unsure. Client intake and triage can reliably route simple requests, but it cannot assess legal merit or urgency beyond patterns in the text. The site tracks 6825 state AI bills, which is a reminder that the compliance rules around these operational choices are still moving.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages in this section form a stack. Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment and Secure Storage and Networking for Legal Data are the foundation, because every other tool depends on where the model runs and how the data is protected. Timekeeping and Billing Narratives and Firm Knowledge Management sit on that foundation, since they both read from the firm's own files and write back into its systems. Client Intake and Triage is the entry point that feeds new matters into those same systems, and a reader would go to it first to understand how work arrives, then to the foundation pages to see how that work is kept private, and finally to the billing and knowledge pages to see how the work is recorded and reused.
